A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PINNMamba work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE-solving experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and computational measurements, including results in Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results, including the appendix sensitivity analyses and PINNMamba results on PINNacle.

M1.justification: The subsequence construction, selective SSM encoder, Wavelet activation, alignment procedure and losses in Equations 21–29 remain unchanged. Correcting an illustrative time coordinate does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same convection, reaction, wave and Navier–Stokes problems, with the same six completed PINNacle cases and the same out-of-memory entries.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: PINN, QRes, PINNsFormer and KAN in Table 1; the same training-strategy combinations in Table 2; and PINN and PINNsFormer in Table 9.

E3.justification: The 101×101 sampling grid, 1000 L-BFGS epochs, subsequence length, loss weights, model configurations and rMAE/rRMSE metrics are unchanged. The PDE settings also match after Appendix D becomes Appendix C.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, loss–error analysis in Figure 9, and length, interval and activation sensitivity studies in Tables 6–8 are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical table entries and plotted findings match, including appendix results and resource measurements. For example, Table 1 retains PINNMamba rMAE values of 0.0188, 0.0094 and 0.0197 for convection, reaction and wave.

T1.justification: The overlapping-subsequence example in v1 Section 5, now v2 Section 6, corrects the point (x, k+Δt) to (x, t+kΔt), making it consistent with the listed sequences. This is a local mathematical correction; the numbered equations, theorem and appendix proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about failure modes, SSM-based propagation, simplicity bias and state-of-the-art performance, including the claimed error reduction of up to 86.3%.

C2.justification: The explanations of pattern propagation, predictive diversity and compatibility with other training methods remain unchanged. Both versions retain the memory limitation on PINNacle and proposed future distributed training.

D1.justification: The implementation information, PyTorch version, H100 hardware, hyperparameters, resource measurements and code/weights access remain the same. Training Details moves from Appendix E to Appendix D without additional technical disclosure.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Related Works moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 2, retaining its comparisons with existing PINNs and data-driven SSM approaches.

P1.justification: v2 moves related work into the main text, renumbers subsequent sections and appendices, corrects 'collection' to 'collocation' throughout, and adds acknowledgements and conference publication information. The remaining prose is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The same 11 figures and nine tables are retained, with changes to placement and spacing. Figures 3–5 receive collocation terminology corrections, and citations and cross-references appear in blue; the plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Corrected collocation terminology and the overlapping-time-coordinate example improve technical clarity, while placing related work before the technical sections makes context easier to find. These are limited presentation and correctness gains; experimental evidence, substantive claims and proofs remain unchanged.
